newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch temp agency Start eyeing foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Dutch temp agency Start eyeing foreign markets.

text.p: Dutch unlisted temporary employment firm Start intends to expand outside the Netherlands, Start chairman Sijbe Attema told reporters on Wednesday.
"We'll try to make acquisitions abroad this year. At this moment, we're in serious talks on several fronts," he said.
For the moment, Start's interest for acquisitions is focused on Germany and Spain, Attema said, adding the company was holding talks with "a couple of" parties in both countries.
Start's expansion outside its present home base is to take place through acquisitions and smaller scale local projects.

An outlet will be opened in the Italian city of Milan in the near future, Attema said. He declined to elaborate on the size of the firms Start intends to buy but said financing the takeovers would be no problem.
"We have enough money to acquire the companies we're now looking at," he said.
Start's balance sheet showed the company owned bourse-listed bonds worth a total of 46 million guilders and also held liquid assets totalling 93 million guilders.
Attema said the expansion plans had also been triggered by the need to ensure the company's continuity.
Start Holding NV's shares are held by a foundation, which is indirectly linked to the Dutch state, employers' associations and trade unions. It has no plans to apply for bourse listing, Attema said.
Start earlier reported a 65 percent surge in operating earnings to 41.6 million guilders in 1996, including 5.7 million guilders of interest gains.
Turnover rose 32 percent to 1.6 billion guilders and net profit climbed 28 percent to 31.4 million guilders.
Start employed about 45,000 temps per day in 1996, some 10,000 more than the daily average in 1995.
The company gave no detailed profit outlook, but was optimistic about its business prospects for 1997.

"Although growth of the temp market abated in the course of 1996, Start expects to maintain and further strengthen its position as a specialist in flexible work forms and as a partner in the area of human resources," it said.

The Dutch temporary labour market is dominated by Randstad and Vedior, the temp agency and cleaning arm of retail group Vendex. Vedior's shares will be floated on the Amsterdam and London stock exchanges tomorrow.
